newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia expels Sri Lankans over illegal entry.
newsitem.headline: Croatia expels Sri Lankans over illegal entry.

text.p: Croatia has expelled four Sri Lankan immigrants who illegally crossed its border, only a week after deporting 145 Kurds over illegal entry, police sources said.
Four Sri Lankan citizens were detained on Friday in the vicinity of the Croatian Adriatic seaside town of Omis near Split after the police caught them without entry visas for Croatia.
A police source told Reuters the men aged between 25 and 30 were caught during a routine police check.
"The police came upon them as they were travelling on a bus. They had no visas to enter Croatia, nothing," he said.
He said they were returned to Bosnia from where they came a night before.
Slobodna Dalmacija newspaper said on Sunday the men illegally crossed the border between Croatia and Bosnia in a private car and they paid $700 to the driver for the service.
"Croatia has become a spring board for illegal immigrants. They want to go to some promised lands via Croatia," the police source said.
The Omis police last week detained 65 Kurdish immigrants who illegally entered the country and another 80 were caught hiding in a Croatian truck in Austria.
The Kurds had been illegally transported to Croatia after arriving in the Bosnian capital Sarajevo.
All were later sent back to Turkey.
Earlier this week Bosnian police cracked down on attempts to smuggle Turkish Kurds to Western Europe after reports Sarajevo was being used as a staging post for Kurdish immigrants.
The Kurds were said to have paid up to 4,000 German marks ($2,500) each to a syndicate which promised them passage to Western Europe.
